gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-noto-sans-ti: Pixel-bright and a bit cheeky, Early GameBoy stretches its spacing wide and lifts its lowercase high, with only a modest thick-thin shift. Noto Sans Tirhuta is plainer, built for steady text.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-noto-sans-ug: Noto Sans Ugaritic reads friendly and low-key, its lowercase sitting close under the capitals with mouths left open. Early GameBoy brings the swagger, so the pairing's best trait is the loud-and-quiet split.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-noto-sans-va: Noto Sans Vai reads in compact, solid word-blocks, with generous space where its curves meet the stems. Use Early GameBoy large for punch.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-noto-sans-vi: Noto Sans Vithkuqi reads open and tidy, its a, c, e and s all breathing freely with barely any step up to the capitals. Early GameBoy stays showy by comparison, and long paragraphs would still feel light.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-noto-sans-wa: Early GameBoy is all swagger and spacing. Noto Sans Wancho counters with a hulking, chalk-heavy lowercase, so the heading does its best work as a flashy opener while the body font is the one that holds up the paragraphs.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-noto-sans-yi: Noto Sans Yi reads modern and businesslike, its deep lowercase midsection and unsealed rounds giving each word some depth. Early GameBoy earns its keep when it's big and brief.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-noto-sans-za: Early GameBoy shouts with spaced, upright letters. Noto Sans Zanabazar Square follows with a soaring x-height and wide gaps, so a long page would feel friendly and crisp rather than crowded.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-noto-traditi: Early GameBoy leads with lively, widely spaced capitals. Its mild dip-pen variation shows off best at display size, while Noto Traditional Nushu keeps to broad, unclosed strokes with bowls that fill the line.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-numans: Early GameBoy plays loud and loose, spaced wide with a small, steady thick-thin shift. Numans runs even looser, its swollen lowercase and far-hanging s ends making a long page feel stretched out and slow.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-onest: Early GameBoy dresses up with lightly engraved contrast and wide spacing. Onest, with its short ascenders over big bowls and marker-like line, can go slightly larger than you'd expect.
